response.text:
Short answer: canceling a meeting is an organizer action that removes the meeting for all participants and usually sends a cancellation notice; deleting a meeting is an individual action that typically only removes it from one person’s calendar and does not notify others.

Key differences (typical across calendaring systems)
- Who it affects
  - Cancel: affects all invited attendees (organizer cancels the event for everyone).
  - Delete: usually affects only the person who deletes the entry (an attendee deleting it removes it from their own calendar).
- Notifications
  - Cancel: sends a cancellation message/notification to attendees (so their calendars update and they are informed).
  - Delete: normally sends no notification to other attendees (unless the deleter is the organizer and the system treats their delete as a cancel).
- Organizer vs attendee permissions
  - Cancel: only the organizer (or someone with delegation) can normally cancel for everyone.
  - Delete: any invitee can delete the item from their own calendar; organizers deleting may be treated differently by the platform (often as a cancel).
- Calendar record and audit trail
  - Cancel: often leaves a record (event marked “canceled”), retains invitation history and may appear in archives or audit logs.
  - Delete: may remove the item from view and possibly go to a trash folder; audit/records depend on system retention policies.
- Resources and bookings
  - Cancel: usually releases resources (rooms/equipment) and updates resource schedules.
  - Delete: if done only by an attendee, resources remain booked; if done by organizer and processed as cancel, resources are released.
- Recurring events and single occurrences
  - Cancel: can cancel one occurrence or the whole series for everyone.
  - Delete: an attendee can remove one occurrence or the series from their calendar; organizer deletion typically cancels the series.
- Recovery
  - Cancel: the event’s cancellation notice and history typically remain searchable.
  - Delete: users may recover deleted items from trash for a limited time (platform-dependent).

Practical rule of thumb: if you want everyone told and the meeting removed for all, cancel it. If you only want it gone from your personal calendar, delete it. Exact behavior can vary by calendar software, so check your system’s help if you need platform-specific details.
